definitions.explanation: A Buddhist sacred text, originally referring to the recorded teachings of the Buddha. One of the three divisions of the Buddhist canon ({三蔵|さんぞう}). Also used more broadly for the chanting of such texts.

examples.japanese: ⟦{僧侶|そうりょ}→僧侶：11529_souryo⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{経|きょう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{唱|とな}えた→唱える：10467_tonaeru⟧。
{般若心経|はんにゃしんぎょう}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{日本|にほん}→日本：03876_nihon⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{最|もっと}も→最も：01736_mottomo⟧⟦{親|した}しまれている→親しむ：14139_shitashimu⟧{経|きょう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{一|ひと}つ→一つ：02948_hitotsu⟧だ。
examples.english: The Heart Sutra is one of the most familiar sutras in Japan.

examples.japanese: ⟦{祖母|そぼ}→祖母：00813_sobo⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{毎朝|まいあさ}→毎朝：00966_maiasa⟧⟦{仏壇|ぶつだん}→仏壇：07116_butsudan⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{前|まえ}→前：02255_mae⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{経|きょう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{読|よ}む→読む：00426_yomu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{日課|にっか}→日課：00317_nikka⟧にして⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧。
examples.english: My grandmother makes it a daily habit to read sutras in front of the Buddhist altar every morning.

notes:
The standalone reading {経|きょう} refers specifically to Buddhist scriptures. The same kanji has many other readings and meanings ({経|けい} as in ⟦{経済|けいざい}→経済：01394_keizai⟧ 'economy,' ⟦{経験|けいけん}→経験：01179_keiken⟧ 'experience').

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {経|きょう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{唱|とな}える→唱える：10467_tonaeru⟧: to chant a sutra
- {経|きょう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{読|よ}む→読む：00426_yomu⟧: to read/recite a sutra
- {経|きょう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{上|あ}げる→上げる：02443_ageru⟧: to chant a sutra (for the deceased)
- ⟦お{経|きょう}→お経：17854_okyou⟧: sutra (polite form, very common)

IMPORTANT SUTRAS:
- {般若心経|はんにゃしんぎょう}: Heart Sutra — the most commonly chanted
- {法華経|ほけきょう}: Lotus Sutra — central to Nichiren Buddhism
- {阿弥陀経|あみだきょう}: Amitabha Sutra — central to Pure Land Buddhism

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦お{経|きょう}→お経：17854_okyou⟧: sutra (polite) — the most common everyday form; used in speech about funerals and daily devotion
- ⟦{経典|きょうてん}→経典：24153_kyouten⟧: scripture; canonical text — the formal/academic term for sacred texts
- {仏典|ぶってん}: Buddhist texts — broader category including commentaries and treatises
